fix(export): Remove redundant hsl() from background color

## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

This PR fixes an issue where exported Images have an incorrect background color.
   - Copied Image incorrectly had a black background.
   - Downloaded SVGs incorrectly had a white background.
This change ensures that the background color of the exported SVG respects the current theme of the editor.

Resolves #1797 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

The code incorrectly wrapped a color value from a CSS variable with an hsl() function, creating an invalid color. The fix removes the redundant hsl() wrapper, ensuring the background color value from the CSS variable is used directly and correctly.

Merge pull request #2029 from mermaid-js/sidv/update-mermaid-12

chore: update to mermaid v12 and derive the diagram theme from its defaults

## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Updates mermaid to **v12** together with the companion `@mermaid-js/*` packages, drops the now-redundant `@mermaid-js/layout-elk`, and replaces the editor's hard-coded `"theme": "default"` with a theme that follows each diagram type's own mermaid default (and its dark variant when the site is dark).

| Package | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mermaid` | `^11.17.2` | `^12.0.0` |
| `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree` | `^0.2.2` | `^1.0.0` |
| `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml` | `^0.2.3` | `^1.0.0` |
| `@mermaid-js/examples` | `^1.4.0` | `^2.0.0` |
| `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` | `^0.2.3` | _removed_ |

Release notes: mermaid@12.0.0.

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

### Dependency update

- **`@mermaid-js/layout-elk` removed.** Mermaid 12 bundles ELK and registers it automatically (it is also the new default layout). Keeping the package would ship a second copy of the layout engine and its `1.0.0` release still declares a `mermaid@^11` peer range. `src/lib/util/mermaid.ts` now only registers tidy-tree, which is not bundled.
- **Peer-dependency warnings.** `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree@1.0.0` and `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml@1.0.0` still declare `mermaid@^11` as a peer. pnpm reports this as a warning only; the upstream packages need their peer ranges bumped.
- The app does not use the removed `defaultRenderer` option or the removed layout-internal exports, and `standardizeDiagramType` already normalises the diagram ids that changed.

### Theme follows the diagram type

Mermaid 12 gives ten config sections their own default theme (`redux-color` with the `neo` look for flowchart, swimlane, agentflow, sequence, class, state, ER, requirement, use case and Venn); everything else uses the global `default`. Pinning `"theme": "default"` in every config, as the editor used to, opted every user out of that.

- **`syncManagedTheme` (state module).** After every validation, and whenever the site switches light/dark, the theme is set to the current diagram type's default — `getDefaultTheme(diagramType)` reads the config section's `theme` from `mermaid.mermaidAPI.defaultConfig`, falling back to the global one — or, in dark mode, `darkVariantOf` it: redux themes get their `-dark` variant (`redux-color` → `redux-dark-color`), anything else becomes `dark`. It converges after one update because the next validation finds the theme already in place.
- **Only editor-set themes are replaced.** `isManagedTheme` accepts a missing theme, the global default, every section default and their dark variants. A theme the user typed into the config (`forest`, `neo`, `base`, …) is never touched, in either mode or when the diagram type changes.

feat: add first-class support for CJK (#8530)

feat: add first-class support for CJK

**Business value**
1. Introduced `Xiaolai-Regular` for CJK as a fallback font for Excalifont
    - it was additionally adjusted to fit our needs
       - removed non-CJK codepoints
       - reduced any Hangul side-bearings to 40%
       - centered in width of inproperly centered CJK codepoints (mainly Hangul Jamo, but also others)
     - it was manually split into multiple woff2 font faces for lazy-loading with https://chinese-font.netlify.app/online-split
1. Improved wrapping to handle CJK codepoints, according to the special CJK rules (especially for Japanese and Korean)
1. Added support for multicodepoint Emojis wrapping (in other words, emojis won't be broken apart during wrapping anymore)
1. Added keyboard shortcut for SVG export (`ctrl+shift+c` on all the platforms) with a toast once completed (similar to PNG).
1. Mitigated subsequent FOUT by fixing local caching for fonts hosted on our CDN (previously cross-origin requests for fonts were not being cached by the service-worker).

Completes #8408

**Technical parts**
[изображение]
https://link.excalidraw.com/readonly/MbbnWPSWXgadXdtmzgeO

1. Improved overall SVG export to process `FontFace`s concurrently (with or without workers, fetching and processing max 3 at a time) with some additional perf. optimisations.
1. Offloaded SVG export in `excalidraw-app` to shortlived `Web Workers` (re-used or terminated after 500ms of inactivity) due to performance issues on the main thread (i.e. just Xiaolai consists of about 250 font faces, which would make the editor unresponsive for a few seconds).
    - as part of this introduced initial infra for a pool of short-lived idle workers (could be possibly re-used elsewhere)
    - added fallback for the main thread in case the `Web Workers` are not available (i.e. running in server-side or when everything is one chunk as in the obsidian)
    - for more fallbacks check the `The NOT so happy path` in the diagram
1. Adjusted the SVG export to inline fallback fonts first, so that their glyphs get overridden by the default fonts. Refactored font and `ExcalidrawFontFace`-related logic and fixed various perf. / caching issues (i.e. bail in font faces cache not working)
1. Adjusted the utils build process to merge all existing fonts with the big CJK font (with normalized glyphs, merged licenses, etc.).
1. Adjusted the whole process for the E+ server-side export (processed on the main thread, fetched dataurl, skipped unnecessary expected logging, etc.).
1. Introduced initial infra for manual code splitting (lazy load **/*.chunk.js in `excalidraw-app`, create separate chunks in esbuild).

Merge pull request #2001 from mermaid-js/sidv/update-mermaid-deps

chore: update mermaid packages to latest & isolate them in Renovate

## Summary

- Bump all mermaid packages to their latest versions:
  - `mermaid` `^11.15.0` → `^11.16.0`
  - `@mermaid-js/examples` `^1.2.0` → `^1.3.0`
  - `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` `^0.2.1` → `^0.2.2`
  - `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree` / `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml` already at latest
- Update the Renovate config so mermaid releases land **fast, in one PR, unmixed**:
  - The old `^mermaid` pattern only matched the bare `mermaid` package — the scoped `@mermaid-js/*` packages were falling into the `group:allNonMajor` PR and getting mixed with unrelated updates. Now matched explicitly.
  - Added `"schedule": ["at any time"]` so the mermaid group ignores the repo-wide `schedule:earlyMondays` and opens a PR as soon as a release is detected.
  - `automerge: true` keeps minor/patch bumps flowing automatically.

## Test plan

- `pnpm check` → 0 errors / 0 warnings (1530 files)
- Verified the lockfile diff only changes mermaid specifiers; remaining churn is pnpm recomputing peer-dependency resolution suffixes (no other top-level dep version changed)
- Renovate config validated with `renovate-config-validator`

feat: do not delete frame children on frame delete (#9011)

feat: do not delete frame children on frame delete

This PR changes how frame deletion works. Previously, we deleted the frame and its children. Now we're only deleting the frame and keeping the children, selecting them instead.

This way it's much easier to remove children from the frame instead of having to do it through context menu in two steps.

If people want to delete both the frame and its children both, they can just hit delete twice.

(Un)related, fixed (or rather, improved, as a proper fix will take more work) selection on removing the last group member when editing a group.
